articles.title: Familiar vs Novel
articles.application_note: Keep familiar behavior for routine tasks; consider novelty when discovery is itself the goal. Compare the learning cost with the intended benefit.
articles.original_exercise: Test a novel gallery interaction against a familiar browse path; keep a clear exit and keyboard route.

articles.title: Onboarding for Active Users
articles.application_note: Teach within the task and make help revisitable instead of requiring a long introduction.
articles.original_exercise: Prototype a first document creation flow with optional contextual help; test it after skipping onboarding.

articles.title: Tesler’s Law
articles.application_note: Distinguish necessary complexity from avoidable burden and decide whether the system can responsibly handle it.
articles.original_exercise: Map each booking decision to user or system; provide editable defaults and a review step.

articles.title: UX Psychology: Google Search
articles.application_note: Use this historical case as a lens for examining search initiation, retained context, result grouping, and feedback. It is not an audit of the current Google interface.
articles.original_exercise: Review a fictional library search with query retention, keyboard suggestions, filters, and empty results.

articles.title: Peak-End Rule
articles.application_note: Map difficult and concluding moments of a journey, including recovery rather than only celebration.
articles.original_exercise: For a failed reservation, preserve entered data, explain the outcome, and offer a safe next step.

articles.title: The Psychology of Design
articles.application_note: Use psychology as design guidance alongside research; avoid turning familiarity, memory, or choice into rigid formulas.
articles.original_exercise: Compare two proposal editors by task success and user control, not engagement alone.

articles.title: Designing with Occam’s Razor
articles.application_note: Question added mechanisms and assumptions; retain the simplest approach that still serves the user’s task.
articles.original_exercise: Compare a plain approval list with an elaborate board while preserving exceptions and accountability.

articles.title: Design Principles for Reducing Cognitive Load
articles.application_note: Reduce unnecessary interpretation and recall while keeping needed alternatives discoverable.
articles.original_exercise: Add explicit labels to unfamiliar icons and show a summary beside a multistep form.
